blocks.text: Hezekiah’s delayed Passover is presented as a restoration of temple worship that reaches beyond Judah. His invitation includes northern tribes as well as Judah, and the celebration brings together prayer, healing, joy, and the service of priests and Levites in Jerusalem. The chapter thus speaks of worshipers and captives from the northern tribes as belonging within an all-Israel horizon, even though the narrative centers on Judah’s Davidic king and the Jerusalem temple.

The messengers’ journey through Ephraim, Manasseh, and Zebulun, and the response of some who come to Jerusalem, should not be read as though the Assyrian conquest made every northern Israelite disappear. The evidence supports deportation, survival, provincial resettlement, and continuing identities rather than the literal disappearance of ten biological tribes.
